title: Tenali Raman and the Riddle of the Two Doors

keywords: the tale of the two doors
full_text:
King Krishnadevaraya, desiring to test the intellectual acumen of his court councilors, constructed a grand philosophical maze in the subterranean vaults beneath the palace.
At the end of the corridor stood two identical heavy iron doors:
One door led to the Royal Treasure Garden of Freedom;
The other door led to the Pit of Banishment.

Before the two doors stood two identical guards:
One guard always spoke the absolute truth;
The other guard always told a deliberate lie.
Neither guard wore any distinguishing badge, and the King gave each councilor permission to ask only **one single question** to **one single guard** to determine which door led to freedom.

Several ministers tried:
One asked: 'Art thou the truth-teller?' Both guards answered 'Yes!'
Another asked: 'Is this the door to freedom?' Both gave contradictory answers, leaving the ministers baffled and trapped in the maze.

Finally, Tenali Raman walked into the vault.
He looked at the two guards calmly. He walked up to the guard on the left and asked his single question:

'Tell me, guard: if I were to ask the other guard which door leads to the Royal Treasure Garden of Freedom, which door would he point to?'

The left guard pointed his spear toward the Door on the Left!

Tenali Raman smiled with supreme confidence.
Without hesitation, Tenali walked over and opened the **Door on the Right**!

The heavy iron door swung open, revealing the sunlit Royal Treasure Garden of Freedom, with King Krishnadevaraya standing there applauding with delight!

The King embraced Tenali:
'Tenali, how didst thou deduce the correct door with absolute certainty using only one question?'

Tenali explained his brilliant logical deduction:
'Maharaj, consider the two possibilities:
If the guard I asked was the Truth-Teller, he would truthfully tell me what the Liar would say. Since the Liar always points to the wrong door, the Truth-Teller would point to the Door of Banishment!
On the other hand, if the guard I asked was the Liar, he would lie about what the Truth-Teller would say. Since the Truth-Teller would point to the Door of Freedom, the Liar would also point to the Door of Banishment!
Therefore, in either case, the answer was guaranteed to point to the wrong door!
By simply choosing the opposite door, I was mathematically guaranteed to step into freedom!'

The King and the scholars marvelled at Tenali’s peerless logical brilliance, celebrating that true reason can navigate through any maze of deception.
moral: Logic and strategic questioning penetrate through deceit to reveal the path of safety.
